thesisQuality.note: Strong product/process relevance and renewed growth support a strong band, but external Foundry value capture remains unproven.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Revenue and operating income improved materially, offset by large Foundry losses and capital intensity.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: September market capitalization near $574B after a sharp re-rating is demanding versus still-unproven Foundry returns.

catalystScore.note: 18A-P risk production, 18A high-volume manufacturing and 14A/customer-demand milestones provide multiple identifiable catalysts, with execution uncertainty.

governancePower.note: Disclosure is adequate and capital allocation is being directed toward leading-edge capacity, but current evidence does not establish exceptional stewardship or returns on that capital.

alignment2036.note: AI/server compute and domestic leading-edge semiconductor capacity are foundational long-duration infrastructure exposures.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Products, data-center/AI and Foundry reuse process, manufacturing and packaging capabilities across multiple demand engines.

bottleneckControl.note: Intel controls meaningful domestic leading-edge capacity and process capability, but TSMC and other foundries remain credible substitutes and external utilization is not established.

scenarioRobustness.note: Multiple product and foundry paths provide optionality, while turnaround economics remain sensitive to node execution and external demand.

substitutionResilience.note: Process roadmap and x86 ecosystem provide replacement barriers, but competing CPUs/accelerators and foundries remain material substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.note: Domestic manufacturing footprint and internal manufacturing capability improve resilience, while leading-edge fab complexity and capital intensity remain dependencies.

pricingPower.note: Current evidence does not demonstrate durable Foundry scarcity rent or external pricing power; large Foundry losses argue for conservative treatment.

risk.note: Material execution, utilization, capital-intensity and valuation risks remain despite operating improvement; Foundry losses are still large.

confidence.note: Primary issuer/SEC evidence directly supports operating facts and an independent current market source supports valuation; external-foundry economics remain an explicit unknown.

thesis: Intel combines improving compute demand with strategically important domestic leading-edge manufacturing; value creation depends on converting process milestones into durable product economics and materially better Foundry utilization/profitability.
keyRisk: The market may be pricing a successful Foundry/18A turnaround before external utilization and normalized Foundry returns are demonstrated.
nextCatalyst: 18A/18A-P production and yield progression plus evidence of committed external Foundry demand and improving segment economics.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore records the methodology-weighted 12-component evidence score; risk and confidence are separately source-addressed for canonical runtime treatment.
